title: Section 2: Body Functions & Secondary Complications (Overview)
source_document: English Master Data Collection & Clinical Content Repository

content.text: Spinal cord injury affects multiple physiological systems depending on the level and completeness of injury:

items: Movement & Motor Function: Loss or weakness of voluntary muscle control below the injury level, affecting mobility, posture, and dexterity.
Sensation: Altered or absent perception of touch, temperature, pressure, and pain.
Bladder & Bowel Function: Disruption of voluntary sphincter control and autonomic signaling, requiring structured management routines.
Sexual & Reproductive Health: Changes in physical response, sensation, and fertility, which can be managed with specialized medical guidance.
Breathing & Respiratory Function: Variable impact on respiratory muscles (diaphragm, intercostals, abdominals) depending on injury height.
Blood Pressure & Heart Rate Regulation: Autonomic vascular control changes leading to orthostatic hypotension or autonomic dysreflexia.
Temperature Regulation (Thermoregulation): Impaired autonomic control of sweating, shivering, and cutaneous vasodilation below the injury level.
